Name: Honoring Pierre Damas Bel and calling on United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement to cease the use of ankle monitors and other body-worn electronic monitoring devices on individuals in civil immigration proceedings with no criminal convictions.
Title: Resolution honoring Pierre Damas Bel and calling on United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement to cease the use of ankle monitors and other body-worn electronic monitoring devices on individuals in civil immigration proceedings with no criminal convictions and to review the existing Intensive Supervision Appearance Program docket to identify everyone that meets that description and remove their devices

History.Description: This Resolution was Introduced by Council
This Resolution was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Immigration

Text:
Whereas, Pierre Damas Bel was a 20-year-old Haitian student living in Springfield, Ohio; and
Whereas, He was a soccer player, a former member of his school’s junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) program, and enrolled in a local public university to study physiology and neuroscience with the dream of becoming a doctor; and
Whereas, Pierre and his family fled the gang violence and political instability of Haiti, and they legally lived and studied in the United States (US) as recipients of Temporary Protected Status (TPS); and
Whereas, Despite the severe devastation and instability still facing Haiti today, in July 2026 the Trump Administration terminated TPS for Haiti making over 350,000 Haitians across the US, many who had legally lived and worked here over a decade, suddenly vulnerable to deportation; and
Whereas, After TPS ended, Pierre was called to report to the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and was forced to wear an ankle monitor as part of ICE’s Alternatives to Detention (ATD) Intensive Supervision Appearance Program (ISAP); and
Whereas, With the ankle monitor affixed to his leg, Pierre became filled with despair; and
Whereas, Pierre began to lose hope and wrote on his Instagram that because of the ankle monitor he was “carrying a shame and humiliation that I never imagined I would experience”; and
Whereas, He was bullied by peers who called him a criminal, and he was no longer able to play soccer due to the monitor on his leg; and
Whereas, The ankle monitor caused him severe discomfort, but in a checkup with ICE the monitor was tightened so Pierre could not put fabric between the monitor and his skin; and
Whereas, Pierre was also witnessing the dehumanizing language and policy changes towards Haitians by the federal government, including the despicable rhetoric about Haitians in Springfield, Ohio, the widely circulated social media videos from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) of shackled Haitian men being forced onto a deportation flight in the rain, and the elimination of TPS and the targeted ICE operations against Haitians in his hometown; and
Whereas, On the morning of August 31, Pierre left his house, where he lived with his family, and took his own life; and
Whereas, The usage of ankle monitoring for cases such as Pierre’s is being increasingly documented; and
Whereas, Under the second Trump Administration there has been a rise in the use of ankle monitors through ISAP, especially for immigrants with no criminal background that previously held a legal status; and
Whereas, According to WLRN Public Media, Haitians in Springfield, Ohio are being specifically targeted for ankle monitors; and
Whereas, The Guardian reported that early in 2025, only 17,000 immigrants were wearing ankle monitors, but as of August 2026, that number grew to almost 54,000 immigrants; and
Whereas, In June 2025 ICE began directing agents to move more immigrants enrolled in ISAP to get ankle monitors; and
Whereas, Advocates and immigration legal service providers argue that ATD now functions as a new form of detention, and that ankle monitors allow an individual to be more easily surveilled and detained on ICE’s whim; and
Whereas, The ankle monitors are equipped with global position systems (GPS) capabilities, can emit pre-programmed audio messages, must be recharged often through a power cord while attached to the body, and reduce freedom of motion; and
Whereas, Ankle monitors have reportedly caused serious physical pain, including cramps, inflammation, bleeding, sores, numbness, electric shocks, bruising, skin eruptions, hair loss, headaches, chest pain, and difficulty breathing; and
Whereas, Those monitored have also shared its detrimental psychological effects, referring to the monitor as a shackle that creates a feeling of being imprisoned; and
Whereas, The hopelessness and despair that Pierre felt, and the pain and agony his family are now experiencing cannot and should not be ignored; and
Whereas, The Trump Administration must not be allowed to use ankle monitoring as another tool in their mass deportation agenda that tracks, detains, abuses, and dehumanizes immigrants and their families; now, therefore, be it
Resolved, That the Council of the City of New York honors Pierre Damas Bel and calls on United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement to cease the use of ankle monitors and other body-worn electronic monitoring devices on individuals in civil immigration proceedings with no criminal convictions and to review the existing Intensive Supervision Appearance Program docket to identify everyone that meets that description and remove their devices.
